surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Olofsson has a goal and two assists as the Golden Knights beat the Mammoth
paras: Jack Eichel struck first for the Golden Knights on the power play early in the first, but Lawson Crouse tied it up for Utah midway through the period. The second period was a wild one. Victor Olofsson scored once and Ivan Barbashev twice in just over five minutes early in the period to put the Knights up 4-1. The Mammoth’s Nick Schmaltz left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Jack McBain cut Vegas’ lead to 4-2 late in the period. Dmitri Simashev made it 4-3 midway through the third, but that was as close as they got. Brett Howden extended the lead to 5-3 a little over a minute later. Three players had three-point nights: Olofsson with a goal and two assists, Mitch Marner with three assists, and McBain with a goal and two assists.
The Golden Knights drove the play, outshooting the Mammoth 28-17, and the scoreboard caught up. Carter Hart made 14 saves for the Golden Knights, and Sebastian Cossa allowed five goals on 28 shots.

The Mammoth killed off a two-man advantage that lasted two minutes late in the first. The Golden Knights moved to 13-5-2, second in the Pacific, while the Mammoth fell to 10-8-1, fifth in the Central.

items.text: Ivan Barbashev passed Alex Pietrangelo for ninth on the Golden Knights’ all-time scoring list, with 188 points.
Four straight wins for the Golden Knights.
The Mammoth are winless in three (0-2-1).
